data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
learningPoints: Builds control of passive voice in formal contexts.
Improves understanding of institutional and official language.
Strengthens grammar commonly used in news and government texts.
Prepares you for reading comprehension in formal documents.
ESOL B2 and aligns with IELTS 6.0–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72–94 score ranges.

sections.summary: Present simple passive for general facts.
sections.explain: Present passive structure: am/is/are + past participle.

words.word: English is spoken in many countries.
English speaks in many countries.
English is speak in many countries.

sections.summary: Past simple passive for completed actions.
sections.explain: Past passive structure: was/were + past participle.

words.word: The law was introduced in 2015.
The law introduced in 2015.
The law was introduce in 2015.

sections.summary: Present perfect passive for recent formal updates.

words.word: The report has been completed.
The report has completed.
The report has been complete.

sections.summary: Passive voice to focus on the action, not the person.
sections.explain: Passive voice emphasizes the action rather than the subject.

words.word: The building was damaged during the storm.
The storm damaged was the building.
The building damaged during the storm.

sections.explain: The agent can be included using 'by' in passive sentences.

words.word: The decision was made by the manager.
The decision made by the manager.
The decision was make by the manager.

sections.explain: Passive voice is common in official instructions.

words.word: Applications are processed within five days.
Applications process within five days.
Applications are process within five days.

sections.explain: Plural subjects use 'were' in past passive.

words.word: The documents were sent yesterday.
The documents was sent yesterday.
The documents were send yesterday.

sections.explain: Passive voice is frequently used in formal academic texts.

words.word: The results were analyzed carefully.
The results analyzed carefully.
The results were analyze carefully.

sections.summary: Present perfect passive for ongoing relevance.
sections.explain: Use present perfect passive for actions with present importance.

words.word: The policy has been updated recently.
The policy has updated recently.
The policy has been update recently.

sections.explain: Formal announcements often use passive constructions.

words.word: The meeting was postponed due to bad weather.
The meeting postponed due to bad weather.
The meeting was postpone due to bad weather.
